semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: "Biomedical engineering" involves applying engineering principles to the healthcare and biology fields, which makes it semantically equivalent to "biomedical applications" as it specifically refers to engineering applications in the biomedical field.

parent_domains.justification: "Biomedical and healthcare" is a broad category encompassing various biomedical fields including engineering, thus making it a parent domain.
"Biomedical engineering" is a specific branch under the broader field of engineering.
As mentioned earlier, it is semantically equivalent, and equivalent domains can also be considered as part of broader parent domains.
"Biomedical engineering" serves as a bridge between engineering and medicine, thereby falling under the scope of "biomedicine" which involves medical science and healthcare.
Given that "biomedical engineering" often involves computational methods, it is related to and can fall under "biomedical computation."

closest_parent_domain.justification: Among the parent domains, "engineering" stands out as the foundational and closest parent domain because "biomedical engineering" is essentially a specialized branch within engineering.

child_domains.justification: As a specialization within biomedical engineering, "biomedical imaging" focuses on developing imaging devices and technologies for medical purposes.
This involves the use of engineering principles to process and analyze biological data, which stems from biomedical engineering.
A subset of biomedical engineering, focusing on analyzing and interpreting signals from the body.
Involves analytical techniques as part of biomedical engineering to understand biomedical data.
This involves engineering sequences which is a technical aspect that can derive from biomedical engineering knowledge.
It is a specific analytical skill in biomedical engineering focusing on analyzing medical images.
Involves processing and analyzing biomedical data, which is part of biomedical engineering tasks.

closest_child_domain.justification: "Biomedical imaging" is closely tied to "biomedical engineering" since it often requires utilizing engineering skills to develop technology for imaging patients, a core task in the biomedical engineering field.

sibling_domains.justification: As both fields overlap and "biomedicine" includes technologies developed through engineering, it can be viewed as a sibling domain.
Functions within the same parent field of "biomedical engineering" but focuses more on applying engineering to solve biomedical problems.
Offers computational techniques and tools utilized within "biomedical engineering," thus exists on the same level.
While focusing on biological data with computational techniques, it shares overlaps with biomedical engineering.
Associated with computational techniques in medical fields which overlap with methods in "biomedical engineering."

closest_sibling_domain.justification: "Biomedical applications" is most closely related as it involves applying engineering solutions to healthcare problems, a core aspect of biomedical engineering.

unrelated_domains.justification: Focuses on chemical processes, differing significantly in scope and focus from biomedical engineering.
Centers more on the educational aspect rather than technological or engineering development within medicine.
More focused on the study of life sciences rather than the integration of engineering principles.
Involves mimicking biological systems rather than applying engineering to medical or biological problems.
While related, "medical" is more general in the context of practicing medicine than developing technologies via engineering principles.
Focused more on robotic systems rather than the broad spectrum of biomedical engineering applications.
